name: Code 777
summary: Deductive game where you see everyone else's tiles but not your own and must infer your own three numbers from questions.
rules_text: Each player has a rack facing away from them containing three number tiles they cannot see. All other racks are visible. Tiles have numbers 1-7 in three colors. A deck of question cards is shuffled. On a turn, the player draws the top question card, reads it aloud, and answers it based only on the tiles they can see on other racks. Example questions: how many distinct numbers do you not see, or do you see more of a specific color. Answers are public. Any player may interrupt at any time to guess the three numbers on their own rack (colors not required). If correct they score 1 point and see the tiles, if wrong 0 points. In either case those three tiles are removed from play and replaced with three new face-down tiles from the draw pile placed by neighbors. When the draw pile gets low it is reshuffled from discarded tiles. First to 3 points wins.
rating_reason: Deductive code rack others see, question cards, perfect hidden info.
